title: Text Is All You Need: Learning Language Representations for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation models dynamic user behavior from historical interactions to understand user preferences.

gap.claim: Existing item-ID- or text-feature-based approaches struggle with cold-start items and transfer to new datasets.

contributions.claim: Recformer models user preferences and item features as language representations intended to generalize to new items and datasets.
Recformer represents each item as a sentence formed by flattening its textual key-value attributes, turning a user item sequence into a sequence of sentences.
Recformer uses a bidirectional Longformer-like Transformer with different embedding layers and combines language understanding with recommendation through pretraining and finetuning methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Recformer as a novel framework and its pretraining and finetuning methods as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on six datasets demonstrating Recformer's effectiveness, especially in low-resource and cold-start settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation models dynamic user behavior from interaction histories.
Existing approaches struggle with cold-start items and transfer to new datasets.
Recformer uses language representations, sentence-like item encoding, sequence retrieval, a bidirectional Transformer, and joint pretraining and finetuning.
The authors report effective next-item recommendation and effectiveness on six datasets, particularly in low-resource and cold-start settings.

source_observation.claim: The approach represents item attributes as text sequences and predicts the next item sentence.

interpretation.claim: A shared language representation may help recommendation systems transfer information across items and datasets.

application.claim: For sequential recommendation with sparse or novel items, consider encoding structured item attributes as language-like sequences and training sequence prediction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach works beyond the reported datasets, item attributes, or low-resource and cold-start settings.

unknowns: The six datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
